name: Rollback Strategy Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building rollback strategy — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary rollback strategy tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building rollback strategy — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary rollback strategy tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about rollback strategy explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Document any non-obvious rollback strategy decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. Measure before optimizing any rollback strategy bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Validate rollback strategy outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. When multiple rollback strategy strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Keep rollback strategy outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Check that rollback strategy terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen rollback strategy approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Keep rollback strategy changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Before starting rollback strategy work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
11. Prefer explicit, readable rollback strategy solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
12. Re-check edge cases relevant to rollback strategy (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic rollback strategy advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of rollback strategy correctness.
- Do not skip documenting rollback strategy assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for rollback strategy, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
